primary_sources: Equal Rights Amendment ratification record, 1972-1982 (Congress, March 22, 1972; Indiana, 35th state, 1977)

source: original; stimulus table compiled from the Equal Rights Amendment ratification record

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the ratification record: Congress proposed the ERA March 22, 1972; Indiana was the 35th and last state to ratify, in 1977; the deadline was extended to June 30, 1982. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 27; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text:
Equal Rights Amendment ratifications (Congress sent the amendment to the states on March 22, 1972; 38 states were needed):

| Year | States ratifying that year | Total ratified |
| 1972 | 22 | 22 |
| 1973 | 8 | 30 |
| 1974 | 3 | 33 |
| 1975 | 1 | 34 |
| 1976 | 0 | 34 |
| 1977 | 1 (Indiana) | 35 |
| 1978-1982 | 0 | 35 |

Congress extended the deadline to June 30, 1982. The amendment fell three states short.

stem: Background: Phyllis Schlafly led the STOP ERA campaign. The table best supports which conclusion about her campaign?

options.text: Her campaign convinced Congress to pass the Equal Rights Amendment itself in 1972.
options.misconception: Congress passed the ERA in 1972, before her campaign gathered force, and her campaign opposed it.

options.text: Her campaign helped stall ratification after the fast start, leaving it three states short.
Her campaign had no effect at all, since ratification sped up after 1973.
options.misconception: The table shows ratification slowing after 1973, from 30 states to only 35 by 1982.

options.text: Her campaign made all 50 states ratify the amendment by 1982.
options.misconception: The table shows only 35 states ratifying, not 50.

rationales.A: Background: Congress passed the ERA in 1972, before her campaign gathered force, and her campaign opposed it.
rationales.B: Background: Schlafly warned that the ERA would harm the family, force women into combat, and end protections in divorce, and after 1973 only five more states ratified.
rationales.C: The table shows ratification slowing after 1973, from 30 states to only 35 by 1982.
rationales.D: The table shows only 35 states ratifying, not 50.
rationales.general:
1. The table shows a fast start: 30 states by the end of 1973.
2. Background: Schlafly organized housewives and church groups against the amendment from 1972 on.
3. After 1973 only five more states ratified, and the amendment ended three states short.
Remember: A sharp bend in a table's totals often marks the point where organized opposition began to work.
